resources.title: Module 1: Limits and derivatives (Synthetic)
resources.text: Module 1 (synthetic): limits and derivatives. This synthetic lesson is written for automated tests and is not real course material. A limit is the value a function approaches as its input approaches a point. A derivative is the instantaneous rate of change of a function. For f(x) = 3x, the slope between x = 1 and x = 5 is (15 - 3) / (5 - 1) = 3. A secant line is a line through two points on a curve. A tangent line is the line that touches a curve at one point with the same slope.

resources.title: Module 2: Differentiation rules (Synthetic)
resources.text: Module 2 (synthetic): differentiation rules. The power rule says the derivative of x^n is n times x^(n-1). By the power rule, the derivative of x^4 at x = 2 is 4 * 2 * 2 * 2 = 32. The chain rule is the rule for differentiating a composition of functions. A critical point is a point where the derivative is zero or undefined. A falling object that drops 5 meters each second for 3 seconds falls 5 * 3 = 15 meters.

resources.title: Module 3: Integrals (Synthetic)
resources.text: Module 3 (synthetic): integrals. An antiderivative is a function whose derivative is the given function. A definite integral is the signed area under a curve between two limits. A rectangle of width 0.5 and height 6 has area 0.5 * 6 = 3. With four rectangles of area 3, the Riemann sum is 4 * 3 = 12. The fundamental theorem of calculus links derivatives and integrals.
